A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LaCoOT. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and compression experiments across seven datasets, including accuracy/MAC results and the block-removal ablation in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: V2 reports original classification experiments, DiT image-generation results, measured computational costs and additional controlled analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The main Wasserstein regularizer and iterative identity-replacement procedure remain. V2 Appendix C adds a limited extension for dimension-changing convolutions: jointly train an alternative average-pooling/1×1-convolution branch through output-distribution matching, then substitute it for the original 3×3 convolution. This changes the replacement procedure for that case.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates classification only. V2 retains the seven classification datasets and adds ImageNet image generation using DiT-XL/2 (Section 5.2.2 and Appendices E/J). Although ImageNet already supplied classification pretraining weights, generating images is a substantially different evaluated task.

E2.justification: Layer Folding, EGP, NEPENTHE and EASIER are retained, while IMP disappears from the ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 comparison. V2 adds comparisons against networks trained from scratch at reduced depths (Appendix H) and SWD, l1, l2, MMD and KL regularizers (Appendix I), substantially expanding the comparator types.

E3.justification: V2 adds critical-path-length, latency and training-time evaluations alongside accuracy/MACs. Its new DiT protocol uses 5,000 finetuning steps and FID on 50,000 generated 256×256 images with 250 sampling steps and guidance 1.5. It also introduces reduced-depth training controls and projection-count/batch-size sweeps. Shared classification training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original lambda/BI/random-removal ablation survives as v2 Figure 4. New analyses examine block distances versus performance, mismatched dimensions, critical path versus resource consumption, training shallow networks from scratch, post-pruning retraining, projection seeding/count, batch size and alternative discrepancy metrics. Appendix E also analyzes generated-image failures.

E5.justification: The original random-removal error bars over ten seeds are retained. V2 additionally reports standard deviations over five runs for Figure 8, three seeds for the random generation comparator in Figure 3, and timing uncertainty in Tables 1/3/4. These additions concern particular experiments; they do not establish increased repetition of the original results.

E6.justification: V2 adds generation, timing, sensitivity and reduced-depth-control results. Figure 3 newly reports FID 56.2 with LaCoOT versus 118.6 without regularization after removing two DiT blocks. The ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 result of 90.99% at 64.69M MACs is retained, now accompanied by latency measurements. Conversely, the detailed ResNet-18/MobileNetv2 result grids for the five other classification datasets are absent. These are additions and removals, not demonstrated version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 Equation 1 inserts the probability weights alpha_i missing from v1's Monge objective, and Section 3.2 restores normalization factors in the block input/output probability measures. The principal Lipschitz, stationary-point, triangle-inequality and gradient arguments remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: V2 broadens the claimed contribution to generative foundation models after brief regularized finetuning. Its abstract also reframes the benefit from almost-lossless removal without finetuning to a better performance/depth trade-off against existing techniques. The central OT-based block-collapse contribution remains, but its advertised scope and performance claim change substantially.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the blanket dimensionality restriction and proposed zero-padding exploration with a tested workaround and future Gromov-Wasserstein direction. It adds explanations of EGP's signal-path failure, qualifications about generated-image fidelity, and the interpretation that distribution matching matters more than the particular metric. Appendix I also discusses SWD's empirical advantage despite the stated theoretical preference for MSWD.

D1.justification: V1 promises public code upon acceptance; v2 supplies a repository link. V2 documents sorting/backpropagation behavior, the unseeded MSWD default, timing hardware and detailed DiT training/sampling settings, including AdamW, batch size 60, EMA and three L40S GPUs. These substantially expand reproducibility information while retaining the shared classifier settings.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work are substantially repositioned around foundation models, scaling, pruning and the practical constraints on fusing linearized layers. New discussions include DiT and Pilo et al. (2025). Dedicated comparisons with distribution-discrepancy and Wasserstein-regularized training literature, including Joo et al. (2020) and Karkar et al. (2023), disappear.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively rewritten. The former Method section becomes separate Preliminaries and LaCoOT sections, with procedure and properties reordered. Experiments gain separate classification, generation and practical-benefit narratives, while the appendices are reorganized and learning details move from Appendix C to J.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the dominant all-dataset numerical tables with multipanel critical-path trade-off plots and adds timing tables, generated-image grids and ablation charts. Figure 1 is redrawn. The retained BI/random ablation moves from v1 Figure 2 to v2 Figure 4 with a reversed MAC axis and shaded uncertainty, rather than constituting a new experiment.

improvement.justification: V1's external-method comparison was confined to ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 and lacked measured runtime evidence. V2 substantially strengthens the practical compression case through broader comparisons, measured inference/training costs (Tables 1/3/4), shallow-from-scratch controls (Table 5) and sensitivity/metric analyses (Appendix I). Implementation disclosures also improve reproducibility. Losing several exhaustive classification result grids reduces auditability, but the new controls and direct efficiency measurements provide a substantial net improvement.
